verdicts.title: Modular Bourgain-Tzafriri Restricted Invertibility Conjectures and Johnson-Lindenstrauss Flattening Conjecture
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We recently formulated important Modular Bourgain-Tzafriri Restricted Invertibility Conjectures and Modular Johnson-Lindenstrauss Flattening Conjecture in the Appendix of \textit{[arXiv: 2207.12799.v1]}. For the sake of wide accessibility we give a self-contained treatment of them.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract describes 'Modular Bourgain-Tzafriri Restricted Invertibility Conjectures' in a Hilbert C*-module setting, with no mention of communication complexity, DISJOINTNESS, sub-column spectral excess, or any quantitative bound that would interact with the specific ξ(M)/CC_R inequality conjectured.

verdicts.title: p-adic Grothendieck Inequality, p-adic Johnson-Lindenstrauss Flattening and p-adic Bourgain-Tzafriri Restricted Invertibility Problems
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We formulate p-adic versions of following three: (1) Grothendieck Inequality, (2) Johnson-Lindenstrauss Flattening Lemma, (3) Bourgain-Tzafriri Restricted Invertibility Theorem.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract merely 'formulates p-adic versions' of Grothendieck, JL, and Bourgain-Tzafriri results; it shares the Bourgain-Tzafriri keyword but does not address sub-column spectral excess bounds or communication complexity of DISJ/PARITY.

verdicts.title: One-way communication complexity and the Neciporuk lower bound on formula size
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: In this paper the Neciporuk method for proving lower bounds on the size of Boolean formulae is reformulated in terms of one-way communication complexity. We investigate the scenarios of probabilistic formulae, nondeterministic formulae, and quantum formulae. In all cases we can use results about one-way communication complexity to prove lower bounds on formula size. In the latter two cases we newly develop the employed communication complexity bounds.
